title.narrative: Unlocking Africa’s Geopark Potential through targeted technical Support

description.narrative:
UNESCO-designated sites—such as Global Geoparks (UGGps), World Heritage Sites, and Biosphere Reserves—are vital for conserving cultural, scientific, and natural heritage. UGGps, the newest designation, integrate geoheritage conservation, education, and sustainable development, proving that environmental protection and economic growth can align.
Despite increasing interest, Africa hosts only two of the world’s 229 Geoparks, with none in Southern Africa. Yet Africa’s rich geological landscapes and cultural diversity offer strong potential. Challenges like limited awareness, infrastructure, and funding remain, prompting Member States to seek UNESCO’s support—especially following the 221st Executive Board session.
In 2022, a FUST-funded initiative and regional workshop in Kenya helped spark growing interest in countries like Senegal, Namibia, and South Africa. The new initiative aims to build on this by supporting candidate countries—such as Botswana, Kenya, Namibia, Tanzania, and South Africa—in preparing Geopark applications, engaging communities, and strengthening institutions.
Key goals include: - Increased understanding of the Geopark model - Draft nominations for at least two sites - Community engagement and capacity building - Enhanced conservation and sustainable tourism UNESCO will mobilize international expertise and foster collaboration through an African Geopark network. This supports FUST’s goals of inclusive development, intercultural dialogue, and science capacity-building. UNESCO’s role will mainly include (1) Technical assistance for nomination files and (2) Support for geoheritage inventories. Potential candidate sites of this project include Tanzania (Kilimanjaro), Namibia, Kenya (Baringo), South Africa, Botswana (Makgadikgadi Pans), This initiative represents a timely and strategic opportunity to advance Africa’s Geopark movement through inclusive, science-based, and locally driven development.
